## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# Object Types & Creation

Object types: Mesh, Curve, Su… [truncated]

Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

61	enum PracticeProject {
62	    static let displayName = "Practice Project"
63	    static let resourceName = "Practice Project"; static let resourceExtension = "framejob"
64	    static var bundledURL: URL? { get }   // Bundle.main.url(forResource:withExtension:)

68	    static func read(into document: ProjectDocument, from package: URL) throws

94	## Approach
95	1. TU-7 in `tutorials.md`: the package `Contents/Resources/Practice Project.framejob`, 1280×720 at 30 fps, three 8 s scenes (Dawn, Sea, Night) each placed as a 6 s clip with 1 s handles back to back on Track 1 (0–18 s, no transition), made by `tools/practice/` with AVFoundation, Core Graphics and Core Text (no ffmpeg); media paths in `project.json` are placeholders that never resolve, re-anchored at open to the bundle's `media/`; opened by `PracticeProject.open()` untitled, titled "Practice Project", clean until edited, so a save asks where and the saved copy references the media inside the app; `new_project {practice: true}` is the agent's door; Help ▸ Tutorials holds Open Practice Project last, TU3 adds page submenus above; `tutorial_check.py` checks needs, media and `SHA256SUMS` (≤ 4,000,000 bytes). 98	4. Generator. `practice_media.swift`: H.264 1280×720 30 fps, `AVVideoAverageBitRateKey` 800_000, BT.709 tags; 48 kHz stereo AAC 128 kbps. Dawn: peach-to-rose gradient, a pale sun rising; Sea: teal-to-navy, three translucent wave bands drifting; Night: indigo-to-black, a crescent and seeded twinkling stars. Each shows "1 Dawn" / "2 Sea" / "3 Night" in Montserrat ExtraBold, white with a soft shadow, and the source time `SS:FF` bottom right in IBM Plex Mono Medium; nothing resembling a person, logo or brand. # MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# Object Types & Creation

Object types: Mesh, Curve, Su… [truncated]

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

While auto mode is active:

You can do much of your work through the Bash tool when it is the simpler route: read files with cat, head, or sed -n, search with grep and find, and make small, mechanical file changes with sed, heredocs, or short scripts instead of the dedicated Read, Edit, or Write tools. The choice is yours: prefer Edit or Write when a shell edit would be fragile, such as exact or multi-line replacements, or sed/awk flags that differ between GNU and BSD/macOS.

1	# Spec §11 — decisions: Tutorials (road map "tutorials")
2	
3	Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
4	[`README.md`](README.md).
5	
6	The road map that makes these is in progress: `designs/tutorials.md` (TU0–TU4), whose
7	"Record" section holds each phase's record. TU-1..TU-6 were recorded in TU0, before any code;
8	TU-2's vocabulary was settled in TU1 and is normative here, not in the road map. The owner's
9	answers of 2026-10-31 (the road map's §10) are marked "owner": the five model tutorials kept,
10	a bundled practice project built now, and the word "Tutorials".
11	
12	- **TU-1 — One source: a tutorial is an ordinary numbered list in its feature's guide page,
13	  and its machine half is an HTML comment at the end of each item.** The sentence a reader
14	  follows on GitHub is the sentence the app shows, word for word, because both are the same
15	  lines; no second set of docs is started, and a tutorial cannot drift from its page. A
16	  heading `### Tutorial: <title>` opens one, and a `<!-- tutorial {json} -->` line under it
17	  names it. Every Markdown viewer hides the comments, so a reader sees plain steps.
18	  `tools/tutorials/tutorial_extract.py` reads every page of `docs/guide/` and the app build's
19	  "Write Tutorials" step writes its output into the bundle as `Tutorials.json`:
20	  `{"format": 1, "pages": [{"page", "title" (the page's H1), "tutorials": [{"id", "title",
21	  "anchor" (the heading's GitHub slug), "needs" (default `{}`), "steps": [{"text", …the
22	  step's machine-half keys verbatim}]}]}]}`, pages sorted by file name, only pages that hold
23	  a tutorial, `json.dumps(indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)`. The extractor refuses a page whose
24	  tutorial breaks the structure of TU-2 (1), naming the page and the line, and the build
25	  fails. Risk accepted: a tutorial's words are the guide's register, written for a reader of
26	  the page, and the coach panel shows them as they are.
27	- **TU-2 — The step vocabulary is closed, and `tools/proof/tutorial_check.py` in `make test`
28	  refuses anything outside it, naming the page, the tutorial and the step.** The vocabulary:
29	  1. *Structure.* A heading `### Tutorial: <title>`; its next non-blank line starts
30	     `<!-- tutorial {json} -->`; then the first ordered list, numbered 1..n; an item's
31	     continuation lines are indented at least 3 spaces; an item may end with
32	     `<!-- step {json} -->` (the JSON may span lines), and nothing follows `-->` in the
33	     item; no `<!-- tutorial` or `<!-- step` appears anywhere else in the page. The step's
34	     sentence is the item's text less the comment, its lines joined by one space; it is
35	     never empty, and its Markdown is kept.
36	  2. *Tutorial keys.* `id`, required, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)+$` and
37	     unique across the guide; `needs`, optional, `{"clip": <filter>}`.
38	  3. *Clip filter.* Optional `has_sound` (bool), `has_pixels` (bool), `kind` (one of
39	     `media`, `still`, `image`, `text`, `shape`, `graphic`, `nest`, `adjustment`),
40	     `follows_clip` (bool: the clip starts at or before the end of the previous clip on its
41	     track) and `has_transition` (bool: its `transition_in` is not null). `{}` is any clip.
42	  4. *Step keys*, all optional: `reveal`, `spotlight`, `wait`, `show_me`, `optional`
43	     (`true`: Skip is offered, and finishing does not require the step).
44	  5. *`reveal`* is `{"tab": clip|media|document|assistant, "sub_tab"?: <a ClipSubTab raw
45	     value>, "section"?: <id>}`; `sub_tab` only with `tab` `clip`; a `section` must be in the
46	     app's target table and its home there must equal the step's `tab` and `sub_tab`.
47	  6. *`spotlight`* is one string: a fixed name of the app's target table, `section:<id>`
48	     (the id in the table), `clip:$selection` or `clip:$created`. The table is
49	     `app/Sources/TutorialTargets.swift`: the fixed names (`timeline.clips`, `ruler`,
50	     `canvas`, `toolbar.play`, `toolbar.timecode`, `toolbar.export`,
51	     `timeline.bar.{split,trim_start,trim_end,ripple_delete,add_marker,duplicate,add_text,
52	     add_shape}`, `inspector.tab.<the tab's title, lowercased>` and
53	     `inspector.sub_tab.<the sub-tab's raw value>` for every case, and
54	     `sheet.export.{format,size,frame_rate,quality,loudness,range,export,add_to_queue,
55	     cancel}`), and every inspector section id the app has, with its home tab and sub-tab.
56	     The checker also fails when the table's section ids and the `id: "<x>", title:`
57	     literals in `app/Sources` differ either way.
58	  7. *`wait`* holds at least one condition, and every one must hold: `selection` `{min?
59	     (an int ≥ 0, default 1), max? (an int ≥ min), …the filter's keys}` (every selected clip
60	     matches); `changed`, a path or a list of paths (a dotted clip-JSON path, met when any
61	     clip selected at the step's start differs there from its value at the start; the path
62	     must resolve in the checker's fixture clips); `clips` `{added: (an int ≥ 1), kind?}`;
63	     `playhead` `{inside: "$selection"|"$created"}`; `range`, exactly one of `{set: true}`
64	     and `{changed: "start"|"end"}`; `sheet` `"export"`; `export_started` `true` (the
65	     sheet's Export…, Add to Queue, or the `export` tool); `playing` `true`. A step with no
66	     `wait` shows Next.
67	  8. *`show_me`* is `{"tool": <name>, "args"?: {…}}`, `{"menu": "<A ▸ B[ ▸ C]>"}`, or a
68	     non-empty list of those, run in order. A tool is in the catalog and not a dev tool;
69	     every key of its `args` is in its `inputSchema.properties`; a literal string where the
70	     property has an `enum` is a member of it; for `set_video`, `set_audio`, `set_text` and
71	     `set_shape`, every leaf of `args.patch`, as `<group>.<path>`, resolves in the fixture
72	     clips. A menu is an item path of the built menu bar whose leaf's selector is a key of
73	     `tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.json`'s `selectors`.
74	  9. *Variables*, inside `show_me` args only, at any depth: `"$selection"`, the clip ids at
75	     the step's start; `"$created"`, the ids added by the latest earlier step, or earlier
76	     call of this Show Me, that added any; `"$playhead"`, a tick; `{"$pick": <filter>}`, the
77	     id of the first matching clip in time order (ties: the front track first);
78	     `{"$first": "$selection"|"$created"}`, the earliest of those ids; `{"$time": {"of":
79	     <ref>, "at": start|middle|end}}`, a tick on the ref's span; `{"$track": "front"}`, the
80	     front track's id, resolved per call (so after an earlier `add_track` call of the same
81	     list it is that new, empty track). A `<ref>` is `"$selection"`, `"$created"`, a `$pick`
82	     or a `$first`. Any other `$`-string or `$`-key is refused.
83	  10. *Menu paths in a sentence.* `▸` appears only inside a bold span `**A ▸ B[ ▸ C]**`,
84	      which is a leaf or submenu path of the built menu bar whose leaf's selector is in
85	      `inventory.json`; the titles are spelled exactly (`Export…` with U+2026).
86	
87	  The checker reads the app's facts from a probe compiled over `app/Sources`
88	  (`tools/proof/tutorial_probe.swift`): the prepared catalog, the dev tools' names, the
89	  target table, the built menu bar and a fixture project's clips as the core writes them. A
90	  probe that does not build is a scored failure. TU1 settled the list beyond the road map's
91	  first draft: `$playhead`, `$first`, `$time`, `$track`, a list and a menu form of Show Me,
92	  `export_started` in place of `queued`, `range`'s `changed`, and the filter's
93	  `follows_clip` and `has_transition`. Risk accepted: a closed list means a new kind of step
94	  is a new entry here and a checker change before any tutorial can use it.
95	- **TU-3 — Show Me does the step the way the app already does it, and is an ordinary edit.**
96	  The tool form, and each tool entry of a list, runs through `AgentServer.execute`, the path
97	  the Assistant's calls take, through the argument gate; each edit it makes is an ordinary
98	  undo step. The menu form performs the built menu bar's own item: validated as a click
99	  validates it, its own action, the path a click takes, and no dev tool
100	  (`perform_menu_item` is not in Distribution). A list runs its entries in order. Exiting a
101	  tutorial undoes nothing. It adds no op and no new way to edit. Risk accepted: a Show Me
102	  edit is in the person's undo history like their own.
103	- **TU-4 — The coach panel is a small non-activating floating panel beside the editor
104	  window, and the spotlight a borderless, click-through child window over it.** The panel is
105	  the recorder panel's kind: it never takes key focus, so typing into an inspector field
106	  still goes to the field; it shows the title, "Step n of m", the sentence and Back, Show
107	  Me, Skip (on an optional step) and Exit. The spotlight is a window, so its ring sits above
108	  the Metal and `AVPlayerLayer` layers, and it follows the target when the layout moves.
109	- **TU-5 — A tutorial's `needs` are checked against the open project before step 1, and
110	  when they are not met the panel says what is missing and offers the practice project.**
111	  It does not start until they are met. The offer names the other way too (open a movie of
112	  your own). A `needs` is a clip filter (TU-2 (3)), so what a tutorial needs is written in
113	  the same words a wait uses.
114	- **TU-6 — The practice project is bundled with the app, its media made by a script checked
115	  in beside it, and it is opened as an untitled copy so the bundled one is never written
116	  (owner, 2026-10-31: build it now).** It holds at least two clips with sound that meet on
117	  one track, room above them for a title, and enough length to set an in/out range and
118	  export it, so every model tutorial's `needs` are met in it, and it is kept so as the set
119	  grows. Its media carries no third-party footage or music, its provenance is written down in
120	  a `PROVENANCE.md`, it is a few megabytes at most, and the product still has no ffmpeg
121	  dependency. Help ▸ Tutorials ▸ Open Practice Project opens it, and a tutorial whose
122	  `needs` are unmet offers the same; it is what the tutorials' proof runs on and what the
123	  videos will film.

  `{"format": 1, "pages": [{"page", "title" (the page's H1), "tutorials": [{"id", "title",
  "anchor" (the heading's GitHub slug), "needs" (default `{}`), "steps": [{"text", …the
  step's machine-half keys verbatim}]}]}]}`, pages sorted by file name, only pages that hold
  a tutorial, `json.dumps(indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)`. The extractor refuses a page whose
  tutorial breaks the structure of TU-2 (1), naming the page and the line, and the build
  fails. Risk accepted: a tutorial's words are the guide's register, written for a reader of
  the page, and the coach panel shows them as they are.
- **TU-2 — The step vocabulary is closed, and `tools/proof/tutorial_check.py` in `make test`
  refuses anything outside it, naming the page, the tutorial and the step.** The vocabulary:
  1. *Structure.* A heading `### Tutorial: <title>`; its next non-blank line starts
     `<!-- tutorial {json} -->`; then the first ordered list, numbered 1..n; an item's
     continuation lines are indented at least 3 spaces; an item may end with
     `<!-- step {json} -->` (the JSON may span lines), and nothing follows `-->` in the
     item; no `<!-- tutorial` or `<!-- step` appears anywhere else in the page. The step's
     sentence is the item's text less the comment, its lines joined by one space; it is
     never empty, and its Markdown is kept.
  2. *Tutorial keys.* `id`, required, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)+$` and
     unique across the guide; `needs`, optional, `{"clip": <filter>}`.
  3. *Clip filter.* Optional `has_sound` (bool), `has_pixels` (bool), `kind` (one of
     `media`, `still`, `image`, `text`, `shape`, `graphic`, `nest`, `adjustment`),
     `follows_clip` (bool: the clip starts at or before the end of the previous clip on its
     track) and `has_transition` (bool: its `transition_in` is not null). `{}` is any clip.
  4. *Step keys*, all optional: `reveal`, `spotlight`, `wait`, `show_me`, `optional`
     (`true`: Skip is offered, and finishing does not require the step).
  5. *`reveal`* is `{"tab": clip|media|document|assistant, "sub_tab"?: <a ClipSubTab raw
     value>, "section"?: <id>}`; `sub_tab` only with `tab` `clip`; a `section` must be in the
     app's target table and its home there must equal the step's `tab` and `sub_tab`.
  6. *`spotlight`* is one string: a fixed name of the app's target table, `section:<id>`
     (the id in the table), `clip:$selection` or `clip:$created`. The table is
     `app/Sources/TutorialTargets.swift`: the fixed names (`timeline.clips`, `ruler`,
     `canvas`, `toolbar.play`, `toolbar.timecode`, `toolbar.export`,
     `timeline.bar.{split,trim_start,trim_end,ripple_delete,add_marker,duplicate,add_text,
     add_shape}`, `inspector.tab.<the tab's title, lowercased>` and
     `inspector.sub_tab.<the sub-tab's raw value>` for every case, and
     `sheet.export.{format,size,frame_rate,quality,loudness,range,export,add_to_queue,
     cancel}`), and every inspector section id the app has, with its home tab and sub-tab.
     The checker also fails when the table's section ids and the `id: "<x>", title:`
     literals in `app/Sources` differ either way.
  7. *`wait`* holds at least one condition, and every one must hold: `selection` `{min?
     (an int ≥ 0, default 1), max? (an int ≥ min), …the filter's keys}` (every selected clip
     matches); `changed`, a path or a list of paths (a dotted clip-JSON path, met when any
     clip selected at the step's start differs there from its value at the start; the path
     must resolve in the checker's fixture clips); `clips` `{added: (an int ≥ 1), kind?}`;
     `playhead` `{inside: "$selection"|"$created"}`; `range`, exactly one of `{set: true}`
     and `{changed: "start"|"end"}`; `sheet` `"export"`; `export_started` `true` (the
     sheet's Export…, Add to Queue, or the `export` tool); `playing` `true`. A step with no
     `wait` shows Next.
  8. *`show_me`* is `{"tool": <name>, "args"?: {…}}`, `{"menu": "<A ▸ B[ ▸ C]>"}`, or a
     non-empty list of those, run in order. A tool is in the catalog and not a dev tool;
     every key of its `args` is in its `inputSchema.properties`; a literal string where the
     property has an `enum` is a member of it; for `set_video`, `set_audio`, `set_text` and
     `set_shape`, every leaf of `args.patch`, as `<group>.<path>`, resolves in the fixture
     clips. A menu is an item path of the built menu bar whose leaf's selector is a key of
     `tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.json`'s `selectors`.
  9. *Variables*, inside `show_me` args only, at any depth: `"$selection"`, the clip ids at
     the step's start; `"$created"`, the ids added by the latest earlier step, or earlier
     call of this Show Me, that added any; `"$playhead"`, a tick; `{"$pick": <filter>}`, the
     id of the first matching clip in time order (ties: the front track first);
     `{"$first": "$selection"|"$created"}`, the earliest of those ids; `{"$time": {"of":
     <ref>, "at": start|middle|end}}`, a tick on the ref's span; `{"$track": "front"}`, the
     front track's id, resolved per call (so after an earlier `add_track` call of the same
     list it is that new, empty track). A `<ref>` is `"$selection"`, `"$created"`, a `$pick`
     or a `$first`. Any other `$`-string or `$`-key is refused.
  10. *Menu paths in a sentence.* `▸` appears only inside a bold span `**A ▸ B[ ▸ C]**`,
      which is a leaf or submenu path of the built menu bar whose leaf's selector is in
      `inventory.json`; the titles are spelled exactly (`Export…` with U+2026).

  The checker reads the app's facts from a probe compiled over `app/Sources`
  (`tools/proof/tutorial_probe.swift`): the prepared catalog, the dev tools' names, the
  target table, the built menu bar and a fixture project's clips as the core writes them. A
  probe that does not build is a scored failure. TU1 settled the list beyond the road map's
  first draft: `$playhead`, `$first`, `$time`, `$track`, a list and a menu form of Show Me,
  `export_started` in place of `queued`, `range`'s `changed`, and the filter's
  `follows_clip` and `has_transition`. Risk accepted: a closed list means a new kind of step
  is a new entry here and a checker change before any tutorial can use it.
- **TU-3 — Show Me does the step the way the app already does it, and is an ordinary edit.**
  The tool form, and each tool entry of a list, runs through `AgentServer.execute`, the path
  the Assistant's calls take, through the argument gate; each edit it makes is an ordinary
  undo step. The menu form performs the built menu bar's own item: validated as a click
  validates it, its own action, the path a click takes, and no dev tool
  (`perform_menu_item` is not in Distribution). A list runs its entries in order. Exiting a
  tutorial undoes nothing. It adds no op and no new way to edit. Risk accepted: a Show Me
  edit is in the person's undo history like their own.
- **TU-4 — The coach panel is a small non-activating floating panel beside the editor
  window, and the spotlight a borderless, click-through child window over it.** The panel is
  the recorder panel's kind: it never takes key focus, so typing into an inspector field
  still goes to the field; it shows the title, "Step n of m", the sentence and Back, Show
  Me, Skip (on an optional step) and Exit. The spotlight is a window, so its ring sits above
  the Metal and `AVPlayerLayer` layers, and it follows the target when the layout moves.
- **TU-5 — A tutorial's `needs` are checked against the open project before step 1, and
  when they are not met the panel says what is missing and offers the practice project.**
  It does not start until they are met. The offer names the other way too (open a movie of
  your own). A `needs` is a clip filter (TU-2 (3)), so what a tutorial needs is written in
  the same words a wait uses.
- **TU-6 — The practice project is bundled with the app, its media made by a script checked
  in beside it, and it is opened as an untitled copy so the bundled one is never written
  (owner, 2026-10-31: build it now).** It holds at least two clips with sound that meet on
  one track, room above them for a title, and enough length to set an in/out range and
  export it, so every model tutorial's `needs` are met in it, and it is kept so as the set
  grows. Its media carries no third-party footage or music, its provenance is written down in
  a `PROVENANCE.md`, it is a few megabytes at most, and the product still has no ffmpeg
  dependency. Help ▸ Tutorials ▸ Open Practice Project opens it, and a tutorial whose
  `needs` are unmet offers the same; it is what the tutorials' proof runs on and what the
  videos will film.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The guide's tutorials as one document (spec §11 TU-1, TU-2 (1)).

    python3 tools/tutorials/tutorial_extract.py --guide docs/guide --out PATH/Tutorials.json

A tutorial is a numbered list under a `### Tutorial: <title>` heading in a page
of `docs/guide/`, named by the `<!-- tutorial {json} -->` line under the
heading, each item's machine half an `<!-- step {json} -->` comment at its end.
This file is the ONE parser: the app build's "Write Tutorials" step runs it to
put `Tutorials.json` in the bundle, and `tools/proof/tutorial_check.py` imports
`parse_guide` and checks the vocabulary on what it answers. Here only the
STRUCTURE is checked (TU-2 (1), the JSON, an `id` string, ids unique across
the guide); a page that breaks it is a `Problem` naming the page and the line,
printed `<page>:<line>: <message>`, and the exit is 1 with nothing written.

The document (TU-1): `{"format": 1, "pages": [{"page", "title", "tutorials":
[{"id", "title", "anchor", "needs", "steps": [{"text", …}]}]}]}`, pages sorted
by file name, only pages with a tutorial, `json.dumps(indent=1,
ensure_ascii=False)`. Stdlib only.
"""

from __future__ import annotations  # the build step's PATH finds /usr/bin's Python 3.9 first

import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple

FORMAT = 1
HEADING = re.compile(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.*?)\s*#*\s*$")
TUTORIAL_HEADING = re.compile(r"^###\s+Tutorial:\s*(.*?)\s*$")
ITEM = re.compile(r"^(\d+)\.\s+(.*)$")
FENCE = re.compile(r"^\s*(```|~~~)")
TUTORIAL_OPEN = "<!-- tutorial"
STEP_OPEN = "<!-- step"
CLOSE = "-->"


class Problem(NamedTuple):
    page: str
    line: int
    tutorial: str | None
    step: int | None
    message: str


def slug(text: str) -> str:
    """GitHub's heading anchor, without the duplicate suffix: lowercased, every
    character but a letter, digit, space, hyphen or underscore dropped, spaces
    made hyphens."""
    kept = "".join(ch for ch in text.lower() if ch.isalnum() or ch in " -_")
    return kept.replace(" ", "-")


def _strip_markup(text: str) -> str:
    """A heading's text as GitHub slugs it: links reduced to their words, code
    and emphasis marks dropped."""
    text = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]*\)", r"\1", text)
    return re.sub(r"[`*]", "", text)


def _comment(lines: list[str], start: int, opener: str):
    """The comment opening on `lines[start]` (which starts with `opener` after
    its indent) up to its `-->`: (json text, index of the closing line, the
    text after `-->`), or None when it never closes."""
    first = lines[start].split(opener, 1)[1]
    parts, index = [first], start
    while CLOSE not in parts[-1]:
        index += 1
        if index >= len(lines):
            return None
        parts.append(lines[index])
    joined = "\n".join(parts)
    body, after = joined.split(CLOSE, 1)
    return body.strip(), index, after.strip()


def _parse_json(text: str):
    try:
        return json.loads(text), None
    except json.JSONDecodeError as error:
        return None, f"{error.msg} at column {error.colno}"


def _items(lines: list[str], start: int):
    """The ordered list starting at `lines[start]`: ([(number, first line index,
    [raw lines])], index after the list)."""
    items, index = [], start
    while index < len(lines):
        line = lines[index]
        match = ITEM.match(line)
        if match:
            items.append((int(match[1]), index, [match[2]]))
            index += 1
            continue
        if line.strip() == "":
            ahead = index + 1
            while ahead < len(lines) and lines[ahead].strip() == "":
                ahead += 1
            if ahead < len(lines) and items and (ITEM.match(lines[ahead])
                                                 or lines[ahead].startswith("   ")):
                index = ahead
                continue
            break
        if items and line.startswith("   "):
            items[-1][2].append(line)
            index += 1
            continue
        break
    return items, index


def _step(name, tutorial_id, number, first, raw, problems):
    """One item's step: {"text", …machine half}, or None after a Problem."""
    def fail(message, line=first):
        problems.append(Problem(name, line + 1, tutorial_id, number, message))

    joined = "\n".join(raw)
    if joined.count(STEP_OPEN) > 1:
        fail("an item holds more than one `<!-- step` comment")
        return None
    half = {}
    text = joined
    if STEP_OPEN in joined:
        before, rest = joined.split(STEP_OPEN, 1)
        if CLOSE not in rest:
            fail("its `<!-- step` comment never closes")
            return None
        body, after = rest.split(CLOSE, 1)
        if after.strip():
            fail(f"text follows the step comment's `-->`: {after.strip()[:60]!r}")
            return None
        half, error = _parse_json(body.strip())
        if error:
            fail(f"its step JSON does not parse: {error}")
            return None
        if not isinstance(half, dict):
            fail("its step JSON is not an object")
            return None
        if "text" in half:
            fail("its step JSON has a `text` key, which is the sentence's")
            return None
        text = before
    sentence = " ".join(part.strip() for part in text.split("\n") if part.strip())
    if not sentence:
        fail("its sentence is empty")
        return None
    return {"text": sentence, **half}


def parse_page(name: str, text: str):
    """(page dict, or None when the page holds no tutorial, [Problem])."""
    lines = text.split("\n")
    problems: list[Problem] = []
    title, tutorials, slugs = None, [], {}
    claimed: set[int] = set()  # lines inside a parsed tutorial's comments and list
    fenced = False
    index = 0
    while index < len(lines):
        line = lines[index]
        if FENCE.match(line):
            fenced = not fenced
            index += 1
            continue
        heading = None if fenced else HEADING.match(line)
        if not heading:
            index += 1
            continue
        words = _strip_markup(heading[2])
        base = slug(words)
        count = slugs.get(base, 0)
        slugs[base] = count + 1
        anchor = base if count == 0 else f"{base}-{count}"
        if len(heading[1]) == 1 and title is None:
            title = heading[2]
        match = TUTORIAL_HEADING.match(line)
        if not match:
            index += 1
            continue
        heading_line = index
        tutorial, index = _tutorial(name, lines, index, match[1], anchor, problems, claimed)
        if tutorial is not None:
            tutorials.append((heading_line, tutorial))
        index = max(index, heading_line + 1)
    for number, line in enumerate(lines):
        if number not in claimed and (TUTORIAL_OPEN in line or STEP_OPEN in line):
            problems.append(Problem(name, number + 1, None, None,
                                    "a tutorial or step comment outside a tutorial's "
                                    "heading line or list"))
    if not tutorials:
        return None, problems
    if title is None:
        problems.append(Problem(name, 1, None, None, "the page has no `# ` title"))
    return {"page": name, "title": title or "", "tutorials": [t for _, t in tutorials]}, problems


def _tutorial(name, lines, index, title, anchor, problems, claimed):
    """The tutorial whose heading is `lines[index]`: (dict or None, next index)."""
    heading = index
    index += 1
    while index < len(lines) and lines[index].strip() == "":
        index += 1
    if index >= len(lines) or not lines[index].lstrip().startswith(TUTORIAL_OPEN) \
            or lines[index] != lines[index].lstrip():
        problems.append(Problem(name, heading + 1, None, None,
                                "the line after a `### Tutorial:` heading is not "
                                "`<!-- tutorial {json} -->`"))
        return None, index
    found = _comment(lines, index, TUTORIAL_OPEN)
    if found is None:
        problems.append(Problem(name, index + 1, None, None,
                                "the `<!-- tutorial` comment never closes"))
        return None, index + 1
    body, closing, after = found
    claimed.update(range(index, closing + 1))
    if after:
        problems.append(Problem(name, closing + 1, None, None,
                                f"text follows the tutorial comment's `-->`: {after[:60]!r}"))
        return None, closing + 1
    head, error = _parse_json(body)
    if error or not isinstance(head, dict):
        problems.append(Problem(name, index + 1, None, None,
                                f"the tutorial JSON does not parse: {error}" if error
                                else "the tutorial JSON is not an object"))
        return None, closing + 1
    tutorial_id = head.get("id")
    if not isinstance(tutorial_id, str):
        problems.append(Problem(name, index + 1, None, None,
                                "the tutorial JSON has no string `id`"))
        return None, closing + 1
    unknown = sorted(set(head) - {"id", "needs"})
    if unknown:
        problems.append(Problem(name, index + 1, tutorial_id, None,
                                f"unknown tutorial key {unknown[0]!r} (TU-2 (2): id, needs)"))
        return None, closing + 1
    index = closing + 1
    while index < len(lines) and not ITEM.match(lines[index]):
        if HEADING.match(lines[index]) or STEP_OPEN in lines[index] \
                or TUTORIAL_OPEN in lines[index]:
            break
        index += 1
    if index >= len(lines) or not ITEM.match(lines[index]):
        problems.append(Problem(name, heading + 1, tutorial_id, None,
                                "the tutorial has no ordered list before the next heading"))
        return None, index
    items, after_list = _items(lines, index)
    claimed.update(range(index, after_list))
    steps = []
    for position, (number, first, raw) in enumerate(items, start=1):
        if number != position:
            problems.append(Problem(name, first + 1, tutorial_id, position,
                                    f"the list is numbered {number} where {position} belongs"))
            continue
        step = _step(name, tutorial_id, position, first, raw, problems)
        if step is not None:
            steps.append(step)
    if len(steps) != len(items):
        return None, after_list
    return {"id": tutorial_id, "title": title, "anchor": anchor,
            "needs": head.get("needs", {}), "steps": steps}, after_list


def parse_guide(folder: Path):
    """The TU-1 document over every `*.md` of `folder`, and every Problem,
    a second use of an id included."""
    folder = Path(folder)
    problems: list[Problem] = []
    pages, seen = [], {}
    for path in sorted(folder.glob("*.md")):
        page, found = parse_page(path.name, path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        problems += found
        if page is None:
            continue
        for tutorial in page["tutorials"]:
            first = seen.get(tutorial["id"])
            if first is not None:
                problems.append(Problem(path.name, 0, tutorial["id"], None,
                                        f"the id {tutorial['id']!r} is already {first}'s"))
            else:
                seen[tutorial["id"]] = path.name
        pages.append(page)
    return {"format": FORMAT, "pages": pages}, problems


def render(document: dict) -> str:
    return json.dumps(document, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--guide", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--out", required=True, type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if not args.guide.is_dir():
        print(f"tutorial_extract: {args.guide} is not a folder", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    document, problems = parse_guide(args.guide)
    if problems:
        for problem in problems:
            print(f"{problem.page}:{problem.line}: {problem.message}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    text = render(document)
    if not args.out.exists() or args.out.read_text(encoding="utf-8") != text:
        args.out.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    count = sum(len(page["tutorials"]) for page in document["pages"])
    print(f"tutorial_extract: {count} tutorials in {len(document['pages'])} pages → {args.out}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

1	// app/Sources/ProjectDocument+Recording.swift — a recording as a new
2	// document (road map 3, phase R1b, the `.newProject` landing; a sequence of
3	// segments since R2b).
4	//
5	// An `extension ProjectDocument` in its own file, `+DisplayStem`'s shape: the
6	// base file is far over the ~600-line cap and takes no code it does not have
7	// to. What it HAD to take is `adoptImported(_:source:fps:)` — `project` and
8	// `importSourceURL` are `private(set)` and `clampViewState()` is private, so
9	// an extension in another file cannot build the untitled document itself —
10	// and that method is `readMediaFile`'s post-probe body moved whole, so a
11	// recording becomes a document by the ONE spelling File ▸ Open uses for a
12	// movie (road map 3, decision 1: a recording is ordinary media).
13	
14	import AppKit
15	
16	extension ProjectDocument {
17	    /// The untitled, dirty document a finished recording opens as — spec
18	    /// §1's opening flow for a movie, with two differences the recorder
19	    /// asks for. The CANVAS takes the recorder's rate (`choice.rate`, 30 or
20	    /// 60 — the grid the person chose) while the media record keeps the
21	    /// file's own, which for a ScreenCaptureKit file is whatever the screen
22	    /// did (R0 measured 25.58 fps at a 1/60 interval; decision 3). And the
23	    /// REMAINDER — a paused recording's later segments, back to back on the
24	    /// first one's track, and every microphone file on a new back track —
25	    /// lands through `RecordingLanding.remainderPlacement` as ONE grouped
26	    /// edit; the FIRST segment is what the document IS.
27	    ///
28	    /// **The order is a contract**, measured on the real class by the
29	    /// document scout and once more by the review, and each step leans on
30	    /// the one before:
31	    ///
32	    /// 1. `openUntitledDocumentAndDisplay(false)` — the controller ADDS the
33	    ///    document itself (no `addDocument`, or it is listed twice) and,
34	    ///    with `false`, makes no window yet.
35	    /// 2. `adoptImported` — with the first segment's descriptor, and BEFORE
36	    ///    anything reads `displayName`: AppKit pins the name on its first
37	    ///    read, and the name is `defaultDraftName()`, which is the
38	    ///    recording's stem only once `importSourceURL` is set. Nothing
39	    ///    between 1 and 2 logs, summarises or shows the document.
40	    /// 3. **The import count** — `fileModificationDate = nil` and
41	    ///    `countEditChange(.changeDone)`, the two lines `makeWindowControllers`
42	    ///    runs for an opened movie (`ProjectDocument.swift`, under its
43	    ///    `importSourceURL != nil, fileURL == nil, !isDocumentEdited` guard)
44	    ///    — run HERE, before the remainder's edit and with or without one.
45	    ///    The position is the fix for a defect the review measured on the
46	    ///    change count: counted the other way round, the remainder's edit
47	    ///    dirtied the document first, `makeWindowControllers`' guard found
48	    ///    it edited and skipped its own count, and ONE ⌘Z brought the count
49	    ///    back to zero — a recording's document that read CLEAN, which ⌘W
50	    ///    then closed without asking. Counted first, the remainder's edit
51	    ///    stacks a SECOND count and its undo leaves the first standing, so
52	    ///    the document is dirty with the remainder or without it, as an
53	    ///    opened movie is. Without a remainder this is the same one count
54	    ///    `makeWindowControllers` would have made, one step earlier.
55	    /// 4. The remainder's grouped edit — named by
56	    ///    `RecordingLanding.remainderActionName(for:)`: "Add Microphone"
57	    ///    for one segment with any voice — its own or a left-out segment's
58	    ///    (#181 item 2) — "Add Camera and Microphone" or "Add Camera" for
59	    ///    one segment with a camera beside the screen, with a voice or
60	    ///    without (spec §11 CAM-10 (4)), "Add Recording Segments" otherwise,
61	    ///    and NOT "Add Recording", because the step removes the remainder
62	    ///    and keeps the first segment's picture, and the Edit menu should
63	    ///    say what ⌘Z will do — before the window, so the `generateCaches()`
64	    ///    inside `makeWindowControllers` covers EVERY file and the editor's
65	    ///    first composition is built once, over the finished project, rather
66	    ///    than rebuilt when the later clips land. Every op was trialled
67	    ///    purely by `remainderPlacement`, so the windowless commit cannot
68	    ///    reach `presentError`'s app-modal arm.
69	    /// 5. `makeWindowControllers()` — its own import count is guarded out by
70	    ///    step 3 (the guard counts only a document nothing has counted, which
71	    ///    is what makes the two orders equivalent for a movie and step 3
72	    ///    safe here); what it still does is run `generateCaches()` and
73	    ///    `ensureReversedMedia()` and add the editor window.
74	    /// 6. `showWindows()`.
75	    ///
76	    /// A throw after step 1 CLOSES the document it opened, or a failed
77	    /// landing would leave an invisible untitled draft in the controller
78	    /// with a blank project in it.
79	    ///
80	    /// **Answers the document AND the remainder's `notes`** — the sentences
81	    /// `remainderPlacement` wrote for each file it landed as media with no
82	    /// clip (a voice too short for a frame, a voice wholly under the previous
83	    /// one, or everything behind a first picture the core refused), each
84	    /// naming the file. A document cannot show a note, and a landing that
85	    /// swallowed them would leave a person looking for a voice that is in the
86	    /// Media tab and nowhere on the timeline; the panel's note and the tool's
87	    /// `note` field append them. Empty when everything landed, and always
88	    /// empty with no remainder. A tuple rather than a property on the
89	    /// document because the notes are about ONE landing, not about the
90	    /// document, and the two callers read them exactly once.
91	    ///
92	    /// Two limits, recorded. With one segment and no microphone the document
93	    /// has NO undo step — its first project is what the document is, as for
94	    /// an opened movie — while with a remainder, ⌘Z (Undo Add Microphone, or
95	    /// Undo Add Recording Segments) removes the remainder's media and clips
96	    /// and leaves the first picture, and the document STAYS dirty under it
97	    /// (step 3's count): the first segment is the document, the rest is an
98	    /// edit to it. And every file stays on disk on either undo, as undoing
99	    /// Add Media… leaves the file (road map 3 §0). Main thread.
100	    static func untitled(around result: RecordingResult) throws
101	        -> (document: ProjectDocument, notes: [String])
102	    {
103	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
104	        let controller = NSDocumentController.shared
105	        guard let document = try controller.openUntitledDocumentAndDisplay(false)
106	            as? ProjectDocument
107	        else {
108	            throw ReelCoreError(
109	                message: "The untitled document did not open as a Frame Job project.")
110	        }
111	        var notes: [String] = []
112	        do {
113	            try document.adoptImported(
114	                result.descriptor, source: URL(fileURLWithPath: result.descriptor.path),
115	                fps: Fps(num: result.choice.rate, den: 1))
116	            // Step 3: the import count, BEFORE the remainder's edit — see the
117	            // doc comment for why the order is the fix.
118	            document.fileModificationDate = nil
119	            document.countEditChange(.changeDone)
120	            if let remainder = try RecordingLanding.remainderPlacement(result, in: document) {
121	                document.performGroupedEdit(
122	                    RecordingLanding.remainderActionName(for: result), remainder.ops)
123	                notes = remainder.notes
124	            }
125	        } catch {
126	            document.close()
127	            throw error
128	        }
129	        document.makeWindowControllers()
130	        document.showWindows()
131	        return (document, notes)
132	    }
133	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

**Playback and rendering.**
- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

  pinned set and a graphic in range. `activeProcessorCount − 1` Foundation

  `svg`, records every report and draws every card (G-8), so the file is
  the serial path's. One `NSCondition` guards everything; a worker never
  waits holding an unfinished entry, so `take`'s wait always ends.

  logs one `[framejob] graphic prefetch: …` line once it is stopped and its
  last worker has exited. A PLAYING preview runs a FOLLOWING session on the
  document's own key (spec §11 G-36, `Playback+Prefetch.swift`): the
  compositor `reach`es each frame it asks for, and the workers skip past it;
  `reach` ignores ticks outside the session's range, a seek's session follows
  nothing until a request lands in its first `armFrames`, a following
  session frees what falls below the floor, and its same-texture shortcut's

  push out the frames drawn ahead. A pass's end line (`done`, `full`,
  `stopped`) is written at its stop. `Slot` lives at the foot of
  `LayerRenderersGraphic.swift` (a pure move under the cap); at 600 lines
  the file's next cut is the background branches.

- `TranscriptReader.swift` · `AgentServer+Transcript.swift` — `get_transcript`

  `filler`, for the assistant's false starts. The cache door reads the cloud
  transcript when its marker serves `.captions` (`cloudWords`); otherwise the
  on-device engine runs over the clip's window off the main thread

  network. The handler's first line reads

  window plus `recognitionPadSeconds` each side (`recognitionJob`).

  language in the package's `cache/device-transcripts/`, keyed by the
  file's source stamp, the language, the OS version and `version`, each run

  stores (dropping runs the new one contains), never after a cancel or a

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library

  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a

  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of `ReelCore.swift`'s
  `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-two op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eight names) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

16	extension ProjectDocument {

18	    /// §1's opening flow for a movie, with two differences the recorder
19	    /// asks for. The CANVAS takes the recorder's rate (`choice.rate`, 30 or

26	    /// edit; the FIRST segment is what the document IS.
27	    ///
28	    /// **The order is a contract**, measured on the real class by the

30	    /// the one before:
31	    ///
32	    /// 1. `openUntitledDocumentAndDisplay(false)` — the controller ADDS the

43	    ///    `importSourceURL != nil, fileURL == nil, !isDocumentEdited` guard)
44	    ///    — run HERE, before the remainder's edit and with or without one.

46	    ///    change count: counted the other way round, the remainder's edit

48	    ///    it edited and skipped its own count, and ONE ⌘Z brought the count
49	    ///    back to zero — a recording's document that read CLEAN, which ⌘W
50	    ///    then closed without asking. Counted first, the remainder's edit

101	        -> (document: ProjectDocument, notes: [String])

103	        assert(Thread.isMainThread)
104	        let controller = NSDocumentController.shared

107	        else {

113	            try document.adoptImported(

128	        }

130	        document.showWindows()

132	    }

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.
